title: Design Database for High-Traffic E-commerce
question: Design a database schema for an e-commerce platform handling 10,000 transactions per second. Requirements: 1) Support products with multiple variants (size, color) and dynamic pricing based on inventory levels, 2) Implement real-time inventory tracking across multiple warehouses, 3) Handle flash sales with concurrent order placement without overselling, 4) Store complete order history with order status transitions and payment states, 5) Support complex queries for reports (daily sales, top products, warehouse performance). Consider: denormalization strategies for product catalog to avoid excessive JOINs during browsing, indexing strategy for fast product search and filtering, handling concurrent inventory updates with optimistic/pessimistic locking, partitioning orders table by date for faster queries, using materialized views for reporting, and database sharding strategy as scale increases beyond single database capacity.

title: Design Scalable Social Media Timeline
question: Design a database system for a social media platform's timeline feature serving 100 million users. Requirements: 1) Users follow other users and see posts from followees in chronological order, 2) Support posts with text, images, videos, and multiple hashtags, 3) Display timeline with pagination (load 20 posts at a time) in under 100ms, 4) Handle celebrity users with millions of followers without performance degradation, 5) Support real-time post creation and instant visibility to followers, 6) Implement trending hashtags calculation. Discuss: fan-out on write vs fan-out on read approaches for timeline generation, denormalized timeline cache tables per user vs real-time query aggregation, handling hot users (celebrities) with hybrid approach, partitioning posts by user_id or timestamp, using Redis for trending hashtags with sorted sets, database vs cache layer for timeline storage, and eventual consistency trade-offs in distributed setup.

title: Multi-Tenant SaaS Database Architecture
question: Design a multi-tenant database architecture for a SaaS CRM application serving 10,000 companies. Requirements: 1) Each tenant (company) has isolated data with zero data leakage risk, 2) Support different feature tiers (basic, premium, enterprise) with varying limits, 3) Allow custom fields per tenant without schema changes, 4) Provide per-tenant backups and data export, 5) Handle tenants of vastly different sizes (10 users vs 10,000 users), 6) Support tenant-level analytics and reporting. Compare three approaches: shared database with tenant_id column (pros: simple, cost-effective; cons: risk of data leakage, challenging queries, noisy neighbors), separate schema per tenant (pros: better isolation, easier per-tenant operations; cons: schema migration complexity, limited scalability), separate database per tenant (pros: complete isolation, independent scaling; cons: high cost, operational overhead). Discuss: indexing strategies with tenant_id as leading column, row-level security policies, handling custom fields with JSONB or EAV pattern, backup and restore strategies, monitoring per-tenant query performance, and sharding strategies for large tenants.

title: Real-Time Analytics Dashboard Database
question: Design a database system for a real-time analytics dashboard showing business metrics updated every second. Requirements: 1) Track user events (page views, clicks, conversions) from 1 million daily active users, 2) Display metrics like total users online, conversion rates, revenue, by various dimensions (country, device, campaign), 3) Support drilling down from daily to hourly to minute-level data, 4) Retain granular data for 30 days, aggregated data for 2 years, 5) Handle sudden traffic spikes (10x normal) without data loss, 6) Power custom reports with arbitrary filters and groupings. Discuss: using time-series database (TimescaleDB, InfluxDB) vs traditional RDBMS, pre-aggregation strategies with materialized views or rollup tables at different time granularities, partitioning event table by timestamp for fast queries and efficient data retention, using columnar storage for analytical queries, streaming aggregation with Apache Flink/Kafka Streams feeding pre-computed results into database, query optimization with bitmap indexes on dimensions, and Lambda/Kappa architecture patterns for real-time + batch processing.

title: Banking Transaction System with ACID Guarantees
question: Design a transaction processing system for a banking application handling money transfers. Requirements: 1) Implement account-to-account transfers maintaining balance accuracy to the cent, 2) Support concurrent transfers without race conditions or lost updates, 3) Prevent negative balances and overdrafts, 4) Maintain complete audit trail of all balance changes with before/after snapshots, 5) Handle distributed transactions across multiple accounts and external payment gateways, 6) Support transaction reversal and dispute resolution, 7) Generate daily reconciliation reports matching debits and credits. Discuss: using SERIALIZABLE isolation level vs explicit row-level locking (SELECT FOR UPDATE), implementing double-entry bookkeeping with separate ledger table, handling concurrent updates with optimistic locking (version column) vs pessimistic locking, transaction timeout and retry strategies for deadlock handling, using database triggers vs application-level auditing for transaction logging, idempotency keys for preventing duplicate transactions during retries, two-phase commit for distributed transactions, and database-level vs application-level balance validation.

title: Location-Based Service with Geospatial Queries
question: Design a database for a food delivery app finding nearby restaurants. Requirements: 1) Store restaurant locations with precise coordinates, 2) Find all restaurants within N kilometers of user's location sorted by distance, 3) Support polygon-based delivery zones (restaurant delivers only to certain areas), 4) Handle real-time driver location updates (thousands of drivers updating location every 10 seconds), 5) Match orders to nearest available drivers within restaurant's delivery radius, 6) Support filtering by cuisine, rating, price while maintaining proximity sorting. Discuss: using PostGIS extension for PostgreSQL with geography/geometry types, spatial indexes (GIST, BRIN) for fast radius queries, choosing between geography (spherical earth) vs geometry (flat plane) for accuracy vs performance, optimizing point-in-polygon queries for delivery zone checking, partitioning driver_location table by city/region for scalability, using write-optimized strategies for high-frequency location updates (batch updates, write-behind cache), denormalizing restaurant data to avoid JOINs during proximity search, and using materialized views with geospatial indexes for complex filtered searches.

title: Comprehensive Audit Trail and Change Tracking
question: Design an audit trail system tracking all changes to sensitive data in a healthcare application. Requirements: 1) Log every INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on patient records, prescriptions, and medical history, 2) Store who made the change, when, what changed (before/after values), and why (user-provided reason), 3) Support querying audit logs by entity, user, date range, and field changed, 4) Ensure audit logs are tamper-proof and cannot be deleted or modified, 5) Retain audit data for 7 years for compliance, 6) Minimize performance impact on main application, 7) Support data reconstruction (time-travel queries to see data state at any point in past). Discuss: using database triggers vs application-level auditing (triggers are foolproof but harder to maintain), separate audit database vs same database (separate for isolation and performance), storing full row snapshot vs delta changes (deltas save space but full snapshot simplifies reconstruction), using append-only audit table with immutability enforced by database permissions, partitioning audit table by date for fast queries and archival, using JSONB for flexible before/after storage, implementing temporal tables (SYSTEM_VERSIONED) for automatic history tracking, and balancing audit detail vs storage cost.

title: Full-Text Search with Ranking and Filters
question: Design a product search system for an e-commerce site with 10 million products. Requirements: 1) Support full-text search across product name, description, brand, category with relevance ranking, 2) Handle typos and misspellings with fuzzy matching, 3) Support filters (price range, brand, category, rating, availability) applied to search results, 4) Implement autocomplete showing top 10 suggestions as user types, 5) Track search analytics (popular searches, zero-result searches, search-to-purchase conversion), 6) Update search index in near real-time as products are added/updated, 7) Return results in under 100ms. Discuss: using PostgreSQL full-text search with tsvector/tsquery vs dedicated search engine (Elasticsearch), creating GIN indexes on tsvector columns for fast search, handling stemming and synonyms with custom dictionaries, denormalizing product data into search-optimized table to avoid JOINs, using database vs application-level caching for popular searches, implementing prefix matching for autocomplete with trigram indexes, storing search logs in separate table with async inserts to avoid blocking, and integrating database with Elasticsearch for advanced search features while keeping database as source of truth.

title: Scalable Notification System with Preferences
question: Design a notification system for a platform sending millions of emails/SMS/push notifications daily. Requirements: 1) Store notification templates with dynamic placeholders, 2) Track notification delivery status (pending, sent, delivered, failed, bounced), 3) Support user preferences (opt-out of certain notification types, channel preferences), 4) Prevent duplicate notifications for same event, 5) Handle retries for failed deliveries with exponential backoff, 6) Provide notification history per user with pagination, 7) Support bulk notifications (e.g., send to all users in a country) efficiently. Discuss: using queue table for pending notifications vs message broker (RabbitMQ/Kafka), indexing notification_queue table by status and scheduled_time for efficient processing, partitioning notifications table by created_date for faster queries and archival, deduplication strategy using unique constraint on (user_id, event_type, event_id, created_date), storing notification preferences as JSONB for flexibility vs separate preferences table, implementing idempotency to handle worker crashes during sending, using database for coordination vs in-memory processing, and archiving old notifications to keep tables small.

title: Content Management with Versioning and Publishing
question: Design a content management system supporting draft, review, and published states with complete version history. Requirements: 1) Authors create draft articles, editors review and approve, system publishes on scheduled date, 2) Track complete version history with ability to revert to any previous version, 3) Support collaborative editing with conflict detection when multiple users edit same draft, 4) Published articles are immutable but can be unpublished or edited (creating new version), 5) Support A/B testing showing different article versions to different user segments, 6) Provide audit trail showing who changed what and when in each version. Discuss: storing versions as separate rows vs delta changes in JSONB (separate rows simpler but more storage), using status column vs separate tables for drafts and published content, implementing optimistic locking for collaborative editing with version counter, handling scheduled publishing with status transitions triggered by background job, using materialized view for 'current published content' to optimize reads, soft deletes for unpublishing vs hard deletes, and database triggers vs application logic for creating automatic version snapshots on updates.
